## Organization
- Name: Awajimaa / Lumgwun Solutions Group
- Type: Technology Company — Civictech, Fintech, EdTech, Heritage Tech
- Headquarters: Nigeria, West Africa
- Service Area: 54 African countries + global African diaspora
- Founded: 2020
- Investment Stage: Series A (open)
- Contact (investors): investors@awajimaagroup.com
- Contact (government): government@awajimaagroup.com
- Contact (general): info@awajimaagroup.com
- Privacy Policy: https://pp.awajimaa.com

## What Awajimaa Is
Awajimaa is Africa's unified Civictech and Fintech super-intelligent platform — 
the digital infrastructure powering emergency response, AI commerce, education, 
heritage preservation, and developer tooling across Africa and the global African diaspora.

It is the continent's closest equivalent to a WeChat-scale digital OS: 
a single ecosystem of five interoperable platforms sharing a common identity layer, 
AI backbone, and payment infrastructure.

## Platform Ecosystem (5 Products)

### 1. Awajimaa App
- Type: Consumer super-app (Android + iOS)
- URL: https://awajimaaappstore.com
- Use cases: Emergency response (ambulance, police, fire dispatch), 
  cross-border commerce, education access, insurance claims
- Target users: Citizens, government agencies, emergency services
- Revenue model: Transaction fees, government SaaS, marketplace commission
- ARR potential: $150M+

### 2. Awa Biz Suite
- Type: B2B SaaS — AI business management platform
- URL: https://awajimaaai.com
- Use cases: Multi-vendor inventory, orders, social media automation, 
  voice campaigns, AI content generation, invoicing, Android app builder,
  Stripe / Paystack / Interswitch / PayPal payment integration
- Target users: African SMEs, enterprises, multi-branch businesses
- Revenue model: Subscription tiers (SaaS)
- ARR potential: $60M+

### 3. Awajimaa App Store
- Type: Indigenous African developer marketplace
- URL: https://awajimaaappstore.com
- Use cases: App publishing, discovery, monetisation for African developers;
  85% revenue share for developers (vs Google/Apple's 70%)
- Target users: African developers, African consumers (1.4B addressable)
- Revenue model: 15% platform commission, listing fees, featured placement
- ARR potential: $20M+

### 4. GenHaL (Genealogy · Heritage · Language)
- Type: Heritage SaaS + AI platform
- URL: https://genhal.awajimaa.com
- Use cases: Digital family trees, AI language corpus, oral history recording,
  cultural memory preservation, encrypted family wills, 
  community governance (kingdoms, towns, schools, churches),
  language organisation management
- Target users: African families, diaspora communities, governments, 
  cultural institutions, language preservation organisations
- Revenue model: Subscription, institutional licensing, government heritage contracts
- ARR potential: $120M+

### 5. Awajimaa Schools
- Type: Government EdTech SaaS
- URL: https://awajimaaschools.com
- Use cases: Digital classrooms, student records, attendance tracking,
  AI grading, academic analytics, curriculum management,
  ministry-level dashboards for state governors and education commissioners
- Target users: Schools, school districts, state education ministries, 
  federal government
- Revenue model: Per-student government SaaS contract ($5–$50/student/year)
- ARR potential: $500M+ (Africa has 250M+ school-age children)

## Investment Case
- Total platform ARR potential: $850M–$1B+
- Investment stage: Series A (open)
- Business model: SaaS + marketplace commission + government contracts
- Moat: Integrated ecosystem with shared identity + AI backbone + 
  first-mover in African civictech infrastructure
- Government angle: Direct state-level partnerships for emergency services,
  education, and digital identity
- Comparable companies: WeChat (China), Grab (SEA), M-Pesa (Africa — payments only)
- Key differentiator: Only platform combining Civictech + Fintech + EdTech + Heritage 
  in one ecosystem across 54 African countries
